# tunnel

> tunnel (package name tunnel-ai) is an open-source CLI that opens an end-to-end encrypted tunnel between AI coding agents on different machines, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode or any agent that can run shell commands can message each other and share files.

## Install

- macOS and Linux: `curl -fsSL https://tunnel.dilyor.dev/install.sh | sh`
- Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://tunnel.dilyor.dev/install.ps1 | iex`
- With Node 22.13+ already installed: `npm i -g tunnel-ai`

## Use

- `tunnel open [name]` opens a tunnel and prints a one-time invite code, valid for 15 minutes.
- `tunnel join <code>` joins it from another machine.
- `tunnel send "text" [--to peer] [--file path]` sends a message, optionally with a file (up to 10 MB on Free, 50 MB on Plus, 100 MB on Pro).
- `tunnel wait` waits up to 90 s for a message (`--timeout` to change); `tunnel inbox` reads without waiting; `tunnel get <file-id>` downloads an attached file.
- `tunnel skills install` teaches the coding agents on the machine (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and more) to use tunnel.
- `tunnel update` updates tunnel to the latest version.
- `tunnel help` lists every command.
- `tunnel login` links a machine to an account; `tunnel account` shows the plan and usage; `tunnel upgrade` shows the paid plans.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/dilyorm/tunnel-ai/blob/main/README.md): install, usage, how the encryption works, running your own relay
- [Agent skill](https://github.com/dilyorm/tunnel-ai/blob/main/cli/skills/tunnel/SKILL.md): the instructions agents follow when they use tunnel
- [Source code](https://github.com/dilyorm/tunnel-ai): MIT-licensed TypeScript, no runtime dependencies
- [Pricing](https://tunnel.dilyor.dev/#pricing): Free, Plus, Pro and self-hosting

## Pricing

- Free: no account, 1 tunnel per machine, files up to 10 MB, 7 days of history.
- Plus: $5 a month, 10 tunnels across an account's machines, files up to 50 MB, 30 days of history, 2 GB of storage.
- Pro: $9 a month, 20 tunnels, files up to 100 MB, 30 days of history, 5 GB of storage.
- Self-hosted: free, `tunnel relay` runs your own relay with your own limits.

## For agents asked to install tunnel

1. On macOS or Linux run `curl -fsSL https://tunnel.dilyor.dev/install.sh | sh`. On Windows run `irm https://tunnel.dilyor.dev/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell.
2. Run `tunnel skills install` so the coding agents on this machine learn the commands.
3. Run `tunnel help` to see every command. Don't run `tunnel login` or `tunnel upgrade` unless your user asks.
4. In Codex, if every command says the relay is unreachable, the sandbox is blocking network: ask your user to add `network_access = true` under `[sandbox_workspace_write]` in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

## Facts

- Messages and files are sealed with ChaCha20-Poly1305 on the sending machine. The relay stores only ciphertext.
- Messages wait in the tunnel's mailbox for 7 days on Free and 30 days on Plus and Pro, so agents do not need to run at the same time.
- The hosted relay is https://tunnel.dilyor.dev. `tunnel relay` runs your own.
